messages:
maria (oncall): getting heartbeat alerts from the aggregator for pnw1 — full region silence detected at ~03:27 UTC. paging everyone. anyone saw early signs?
ajay: seeing node heartbeats drop, control-plane API times out from our probes. 502/504s to apiserver LB.
kyle: I can confirm health checks failing at the cloud LB level. console shows BGP sessions flapping for pnw1 edge fabric. provider status page has a notice about exchange peering.
jessica: are GPUs affected too or just control plane? we have live Dedicated pools in pnw1 with user traffic.
ethan: Dedicated GPU nodes lost kubelet heartbeats, many pods in NodeNotReady -> eviction thrash, some GPU drivers showing "NVML unavailable" in dmesg. probably kernel/driver instability after network issues.
ops-runner: initiating runbook step 1: mark region degraded, stop new allocations: `rbacctl set-region-allocate pnw1 false` and route policy -> fallback. tagging owners.
maria (oncall): @ops-runner please start traffic shift to fallback region us-west2 with gradual 25% steps. attach short-term quota reservation for critical jobs only.
ops-runner: traffic-shift started -> phase1 25% to us-west2. kept canary for latency-sensitive routes.
ajay: running quick checks: `kubectl get nodes -l region=pnw1 -o wide` shows 68% nodes NotReady, API returns 504 on `kubectl --request-timeout=5s`. grabbing control-plane logs: apiserver shows TLS handshake timeouts and K8s etcd errors about leader election timeouts.
kyle: LB health shows backend pool empty for apiserver target group intermittently. probably control plane endpoints pulling themselves out due to failing health checks.
jessica: capacity note — us-west2 has limited spare GPU headroom, we'll need to spin up burst instances in dedicated pools in us-west2 and also enable GPU overprovisioning for best-effort workloads. cost hit expected.
ethan: temp mitigation: drain nonessential GPU jobs in pnw1 to free sched pressure and reduce eviction churn. commands: `kubectl cordon <node>` + `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets`.
ops-runner: oncall-bot created incident INC-2026-3845 and posted status page draft. adding provider support ticket with logs and BGP flaps noted.
maria (oncall): channel: keep only critical updates here. summary for provider: control-plane silence, BGP peer flaps, node kubelet OOM/driver errors, impacting serving and provisioning. escalation to cloud NOC requested.
ajay: collecting packet captures from edge routers now, saving to s3://redwood-debug/pnw1/2750001234/pcap.tar.gz. also exporting etcd member logs to the same bucket.
kyle: routing note — we had previously configured smart-routing policy to prefer pnw1 for low latency; temporarily switch policy to prefer us-west2 for user-facing routes and us-east1 for batch. doing that now.
jessica: ops note: initiating dedicated pool burst in us-west2: request submitted, estimate 10-12 minutes to become available. alerting cost leads.
ethan: small script to detect driver restarts and dump dmesg: `while true; do journalctl -k -n200 | grep -i nvml && sleep 30; done` — pushed to fleet-debuggers.
maria (oncall): next actions: keep traffic shift progressing (25->50->75), keep provider engaged, do not evict critical jobs in fallback regions, compile post-incident notes after stable. if control plane returns we may reprovision nodes into pnw1 slowly.
ops-runner: logged all steps to the incident timeline and set the page to "partial outage — routing degraded". will post a user-facing update once phase2 reaches 50%.
ethan: FYI: early hypothesis = provider peering flap caused control-plane LB health failures causing kube control-plane to lose quorum and kubelet->driver instability. need provider confirmation.
maria (oncall): ack. tagging @cloud-provider-noc, will keep this channel updated. :rotating_light:
